pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING ALOUD

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: MANDARIN
Strand: READING THEME 1: GREETINGS AND INTRODUCTION Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning 
Topic 2.2: Reading Aloud

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading Aloud. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is reading aloud important?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify key words and phrases from a reading text
2. appreciate the importance of reading aloud in oral communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING ALOUD
Subject: MANDARIN · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading Aloud helps you succeed in MANDARIN. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING ALOUD
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify key words and phrases from a reading text

What this means
In this part you learn to identify key words and phrases from a reading text. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify key words and phrases from a reading text.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading Aloud”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify key words and phrases from a reading text. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the importance of reading aloud in oral communication

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of reading aloud in oral communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of reading aloud in oral communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading Aloud to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of reading aloud in oral communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading Aloud is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading Aloud”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify key words and phrases from a reading text)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading Aloud to a partner. (skill: appreciate the importance of reading aloud in oral communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading Aloud to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify key words and phrases from a reading text.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the importance of reading aloud in oral communication.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading Aloud from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading Aloud: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Reading Aloud?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is reading aloud important?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading Aloud means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify key words and phrases from a reading text.
5. Be able to: appreciate the importance of reading aloud in oral communication.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
